names.D: 教師指引、參考答案及評分準則

steps: 本工作紙按 proposal 4.1 及 4.3.2 提供相同情境、概念、題幹及靜態資料；活動在正式授課前進行。每週工作紙與正式 10 題 SPSAI、4 題 CKT 前後測分開。
先派 A，保存原始觀察、假說、理由、變量、前提及裝置設計；保留可供學生反思參閱的副本。
原始設計保存後才派 B。以同一四裝置、四時間點的靜態圖取代互動；讀數、計算、圖表及結論由學生完成。
保存首次讀數；修訂另記，讓原答案保持可讀。固定原探究答案後才派 C，不預先揭示學習重點。
學生參閱 A 的原始假說及理由，在 C 完成相同反思。D 及完整套裝只供教師，分冊派發。
兩組使用相同情境、問題、提示、資料、語言及可用時間。靜態閱讀與數位操作是處理方式差異，不能把紙本完成率當作操作能力。
目前 VL2 沒有延伸探究，紙本不加入額外題目。正式研究前後測與本次活動工作紙分開。
正式派發前試印 B 和 C 的灰階圖，確認水面、紅色水跡、量尺及科學標籤可讀。用時、點擊及完成率不直接換算 SPS 分數。

context.note:
西芹長柄（葉柄）

這部分外觀像莖，內含木質部，可讓我們觀察水分向上運輸。留意：它在植物構造上屬於葉柄。
context.caption: 示意圖以虛擬剖視呈現內部水跡，實驗樣本並沒有被縱向切開。
context.taskTitle: 紅色水跡，藏着甚麼線索？
paragraphs: 園藝小組把帶葉西芹插入紅色水中，並在一段時間前後觀察西芹。
請先觀察左方兩個圖像，記錄你看到的變化。他們想知道：光照和葉片會否影響水分運輸？
context.question:
主要探究問題

在其他條件相同下，光強度如何影響帶葉西芹中紅色水跡向上移動的速度？

observation.label: 你的初步觀察
observation.hint: 你看到甚麼變化？先描述現象，暫時不用解釋原因。

hypothesis.heading: 完成你的預測
hypothesis.sentence: 若光強度增加，紅色水跡向上移動的速度將會 __________。
hypothesis.hint: 寫下你的想法；預測沒有必須猜中的答案。

variables.heading: 辨認實驗變量
variables.instruction: 在每類中選擇適合的因素。現在保存你的想法，遞交後再查看參考回饋。

choices.text: 光強度

choices.id: 紅色水跡上升高度／平均上移速度
choices.text: 紅色水跡上升高度／平均上移速度
溫度

choices.text: 紅色水濃度及浸入深度

choices.id: 西芹長柄的長度及粗幼
choices.text: 西芹長柄的長度及粗幼

assumptions.heading: 此探究的假設是什麼？
assumptions.reminder: 假設是指未經證實而被視為正確的條件，用於確保實驗結果的有效性。
assumptions.instruction: 請選出所有適用的假設，可選多於一項。

choices.text: 改變燈距不會造成各裝置溫度不同。
裝置A、裝置B、裝置C 的總葉面積相同。
葉面積不會影響結果，因此毋須控制。
各裝置的濕度及氣流相同。

control.heading: 探究的對照組
control.question: 若想知道葉片是否參與水分運輸，你會如何設計比較裝置？
hints: （提示：對照組主要功能是作為比較的基準，用來確認實驗中的改變是由獨立變量所引起，而非其他外在因素的干擾，因此對照組不包含獨立變量的處理條件）
（提示：此對照裝置與實驗裝置有何不同之處？）

design.heading: 繪畫並標示你的四個裝置
design.reminder: 不用精緻地繪畫所有特徵，簡單繪畫並標示清楚便可。
design.instruction: 包括西芹、葉片、紅色水、燈具、距離及量度位置。每株西芹浸入紅色水 2 cm。
design.hint: 可補充繪圖標示，或以文字完整描述四個裝置，作為繪圖的替代。

experiment.heading: 進行探究與收集數據
experiment.instruction: 四個裝置同步運行；每 10 分鐘模擬時間進行一次量度。
experiment.conditions: ✦固定條件：溫度 25°C、相同濕度及氣流、相同紅色水濃度、2 cm 浸入深度，以及相近的長柄長度與粗幼。裝置A、裝置B、裝置C 的總葉面積相同；裝置D 沒有葉片。
experiment.timing: 真實實驗提醒：量度時應讓實驗和計時持續進行，並在預定時間迅速讀取及記錄數據，不應為了量度而停止計時。本模擬暫停畫面，方便你觀察和記錄；這段操作時間不計入模擬的 30 分鐘。
ruler: 按住尺子左右移動到長柄旁。尺子的 0 刻度已固定在水面位置，不能上下移動。讀取紅色水跡頂端的高度，輸入數據並保留一位小數。讀數旁的箭嘴每次增減 0.5 cm。
每段 10 分鐘模擬時間會加速至約 3 秒。這是教學模型，並非真實實驗的精確預測。

questions.sentence: 我們只量度了紅色水跡的高度，沒有量度葉片散失的水汽。以下哪個說法最恰當？__________

options.text: 紅色水跡可作為植物吸水及水分向上運輸的線索，不能代表葉片蒸發水分的速度，即蒸騰速率。
水跡上移速度就是葉片散失水汽的速率，可直接當作蒸騰速率。
只要帶葉組比不帶葉組快，就已完全證明水汽只經氣孔散失。

learning.heading: 從紅色水跡，認識蒸騰
learning.points:
1. 蒸騰是植物體內的水份蒸發，並以水汽形式散失到大氣的過程。水汽主要經葉和草本莖上的氣孔散失。
    1. 水份從葉肉細胞表面的水膜蒸發成水汽，進入海綿葉肉中的氣室。當氣室的水汽濃度高於外界大氣，水汽便經氣孔藉擴散離開葉。
    2. 葉肉細胞散失水份後，水勢下降，並藉滲透從鄰近細胞吸收水份。水份因而從葉的木質導管被抽出，產生蒸騰拉力，把水份沿莖的木質導管向上牽引。
  2. 在水份供應充足等合適條件下，較高的光強度通常使氣孔張得更大，水汽藉擴散離開葉的速率加快，蒸騰速率因而上升。
    注意：增加光照亦可能使葉的溫度上升，進一步加快蒸騰。因此，此探究假設所有裝置的溫度相同，以便比較光強度的影響。
  3. 蒸騰拉力促使根持續吸收水份，並驅使水份和根吸收的已溶解礦物質沿木質導管向上轉運到葉。
learning.limit: 參照課本第 11.1 節，頁 11-3 至 11-8。紅色水跡顯示水分運輸的線索，不能直接等同蒸騰速率；帶葉／不帶葉比較亦不能單獨證明氣孔的作用。

cards.text: 水份從葉肉細胞表面蒸發，並進入氣室中。
氣室內的水汽經氣孔擴散到大氣中。
水份從葉肉細胞散失，細胞的水勢因而下降。
葉肉細胞藉滲透從鄰近細胞吸收水份。
木質導管內的水被抽出，形成蒸騰拉力。

caption: 葉的內部構造與蒸騰

texts.observation: 過了一段時間後，紅色水跡沿西芹長柄內的部分區域向上延伸。
texts.hypothesis: 此題沒有固定答案；假說應能透過改變光強度和量度水跡上移速度來測試。
texts.reason: 說明你預期光照與水分運輸有何關係；預測毋須猜中結果。
texts.control: 裝置D 不帶葉，與帶葉的裝置B 比較；兩者皆為 20 cm 光照距離，其餘條件相同，主要差別是葉片有無。
texts.design: 材料：西芹 ×4、檯燈 ×4、紅色水杯 ×4、30 cm 尺子 ×4、剪刀 ×1、計時器 ×1。三株帶葉西芹的燈距為 10、20、30 cm；不帶葉組與其中一個帶葉組保持相同燈距。各浸入紅色水 2 cm。

assumptions.text: 改變燈距不會造成各裝置溫度不同。
assumptions.reference: 溫度亦可能影響蒸騰。此模擬維持各裝置 25°C，避免光照與溫度同時改變。

assumptions.text: 裝置A、裝置B、裝置C 的總葉面積相同。
assumptions.reference: 葉面積可能影響水分散失，因此帶葉組裝置A、裝置B、裝置C 應保持相同總葉面積；不帶葉的裝置D 是另一項比較。

assumptions.text: 葉面積不會影響結果，因此毋須控制。
assumptions.reference: 不能把葉面積視為沒有影響；它可能影響水分散失，光照比較中需要控制。

assumptions.text: 各裝置的濕度及氣流相同。
assumptions.reference: 濕度及氣流亦可能影響蒸騰，因此比較光照時應保持相同。

明確預測改變光強度後水跡速度如何改變，並給出與現象相關的理由；不要求預測結果正確。
1：假說可測試，但理由缺漏或不清晰。
沒有可測試的假說；只抄結論而無實驗前預測。
實驗假設選擇
自動
只選溫度不改變、帶葉組總葉面積相同、濕度及氣流相同三項。
全組正確才給分；不另計部分分。
錯選、漏選或未作答。
對照裝置設計
教師填寫
帶葉／不帶葉裝置使用相同燈距，其餘條件保持相同。
此項只給 0 或 1 分。
沒有控制葉片以外的因素，或未作答。
四輪完整量度
自動
0、10、20、30 min 各有四個有效、已確認讀數。
每輪 0.5；量度準確度另計於觀察，不重複計。
沒有完整確認的量度輪次。
實驗裝置方案
教師填寫
圖像／文字顯示四株、三種帶葉燈距及同距不帶葉對照、紅色水及量尺／時間量度安排。
1：方案基本可操作，但缺少一項主要安排。
不能操作、無關或未完成。
平均上移速度計算
自動
四組（30 min 高度 − 0 min 高度）÷ 30；每組正確 0.5。
依學生最後確認讀數計算，新紀錄保留兩位小數，允許 0.0051 cm/min 捨入差異；舊紀錄依原有三位小數及 0.00051 容差檢核。
無正確計算；不使用模型高度取代學生讀數評算術。
四項結論
自動
光強度增加速度通常增加；B/D 比較與學生計算相符；葉片促進運輸；水跡為間接線索。
每個正確選項 0.5。B/D 資料不足不得分。
錯誤／未回答。
圖表標點及連線
自動
四點 X = 各組 lux、Y = 學生自己計算速度（每點 0.375）；正確 A/B/C 三點已連線（0.5）。
以未四捨五入的點數計分再保留兩位小數；不把 D 連入帶葉曲線。
無正確標點或連線。計算錯誤另計於推論，圖表以其計算檢核。
書面表達
教師填寫
觀察、裝置方案及反思能清楚傳達想法，數據／裝置名稱／單位使用清晰；評表達而非概念正確性。
1：可理解，但描述含糊或缺乏必要標示。
無法理解或未提供可評的表達。
學習反思：蒸騰與氣孔
教師填寫
修訂解釋中正確說明葉肉細胞表面水膜蒸發，水汽經氣孔擴散離開葉。
1：正確提及葉片蒸發／氣孔散失水汽，但機制不完整。
未用此概念或有核心錯誤。
學習反思：木質部及蒸騰拉力
教師填寫
修訂解釋中連結蒸騰產生蒸騰拉力，使水份沿木質導管向上運輸。
1：正確提及木質部運輸或蒸騰拉力，但沒有連結。
未用此概念或有核心錯誤。
學習反思：光強度影響
教師填寫
修訂解釋中連結較強光照通常促進氣孔開啟、蒸騰及水分向上運輸，避免稱水跡速度就是蒸騰速率。
1：正確描述較強光照與較快水跡的關係，但沒有機制。
關係相反、直接等同蒸騰速率或未運用概念。
學習反思：運用概念修訂原始解釋
教師填寫
指出原始假說是否獲自己數據支持，以數據及學習重點修訂／完善解釋；原始假說正確也可得滿分。
1：有判斷或修訂，但欠缺數據／概念連結。
只抄學習重點，未檢驗原始假說，或未提交反思。
配分與完成條件
公式彙總
六項 SPS 各 4 分，共 24；新知識四項各 2，共 8；整體 32。教師填完九個評分格及學生完成反思，整體分數才顯示。
人工評分格空白＝待評，與填 0 分不同。公式由 Excel 開啟時重算；教師在此檔填分後請保存。
新下載 Excel 不會讀取之前檔案內的人工分數；分數只存於教師保存的 Excel。
色彩與研究使用
說明
底色區分 SPS 類別及新知識；綠字正確／滿分，紅字錯誤／零分，橙字部分得分，未評中性色。
人工答案在填分後依公式變色。PDF 不顯示任何分數；活動紀錄不是 SPS 分數。
本 rubric 為 VL2 初稿；正式縱向比較前需對四個模組統一準則、配分及評分者校準。

names.D: Teacher guide, answers and scoring guide

steps: Following proposal 4.1 and 4.3.2, these worksheets use the same scenarios, concepts, prompts and static data, before formal teaching. Keep weekly worksheets separate from the formal 10-item SPSAI and 4-item CKT pre- and post-tests.
Give out A first. Save the original observation, hypothesis, reason, variables, assumptions and setup design. Keep a copy students can consult during reflection.
Give out B after saving the original design. Static images replace interaction for the same four setups and four times. Students complete the readings, calculations, graph and conclusions.
Keep first readings legible and record revisions separately. Give out C only after the original investigation answers are fixed; do not reveal the learning points earlier.
Students consult their original hypothesis and reason in A and complete the same reflection in C. D and the full pack are for teachers only; distribute the parts separately.

Use the same situation, questions, hints, data, language and available time for both groups. Static reading and digital interaction are different treatments; paper completion is not a measure of operating skill.
The current VL2 has no extension investigation; the paper does not add one. Keep formal research pre- and post-tests separate from these activity worksheets.
Test-print B and C in grayscale before use. Check liquid surfaces, water traces, rulers and scientific labels. Time, clicks and completion rate do not directly become SPS scores.

context.note:
Celery leaf stalk (petiole (葉柄))

This part looks like a stem. It contains xylem (木質部), so we can observe water moving upwards. It is a leaf stalk, called a petiole (葉柄).
context.caption: This diagram shows an imaginary cutaway so you can see the water trace inside. The celery used in the experiment has not been cut lengthwise.
context.taskTitle: What can the red water trace tell us?
paragraphs: The gardening group puts celery with leaves in red water. They observe it before and after some time has passed.
Look at the two pictures on the left and record the changes you see. The group wants to know: do light and leaves affect water transport?
context.question:
Main investigation question

When other conditions are the same, how does light intensity (光強度) affect the upward speed of the red water trace in celery with leaves?

observation.label: Your first observations
observation.hint: What changes do you see? Describe them first. You do not need to explain why yet.

hypothesis.heading: Complete your prediction
hypothesis.sentence: If light intensity (光強度) increases, the upward speed of the red water trace will __________.
hypothesis.hint: Write your ideas. Your prediction does not have to match the expected result.

variables.heading: Identify the variables
variables.instruction: Choose the factors that fit each variable type. Save your ideas now. You can view feedback after you submit.

choices.text: Light intensity (光強度)

choices.id: 紅色水跡上升高度／平均上移速度
choices.text: Height / average upward speed of the red water trace
Temperature
Humidity (濕度) and air movement

choices.id: 紅色水濃度及浸入深度
choices.text: Red water concentration and depth of immersion (浸入深度)
Total leaf area of the setups with leaves

choices.id: 西芹長柄的長度及粗幼
choices.text: Length and thickness of the celery stalks

assumptions.heading: What assumptions does this investigation make?
assumptions.reminder: An assumption is a condition we have not proved but take as true, to help make the experiment results valid.
assumptions.instruction: Choose all the assumptions that apply. You may choose more than one.

choices.text: Changing the lamp distance does not make the setups have different temperatures.
Setups A, B and C have the same total leaf area.
Leaf area does not affect the results, so it does not need to be kept the same.
Humidity (濕度) and air movement are the same for all setups.

control.heading: The control group
control.question: How would you plan a comparison setup to find out whether leaves help with water transport?
hints: (Hint: the control group provides a basis for comparison. It helps check whether the change in the experiment is caused by the independent variable rather than other external factors. The control group therefore does not receive the treatment being tested.)
(Hint: how is the control setup different from the experiment setup?)

design.heading: Draw and label your four setups
design.reminder: You do not need to draw every detail carefully. A simple drawing with clear labels is enough.
design.instruction: Include the celery, leaves, red water, lamps, distances and measurement positions. Put 2 cm of each celery leaf stalk into the red water.
design.hint: Add labels for your drawing, or describe all four setups in words instead of drawing them.

experiment.heading: Carry out the investigation and collect data
experiment.instruction: All four setups run together. Take measurements every 10 minutes of simulated time.
experiment.conditions: ✦Conditions kept the same: Temperature of 25°C, the same humidity (濕度) and air flow, the same red water concentration, a depth of 2 cm in the water, and leaf stalks of similar length and thickness. Setups A, B and C have the same total leaf area. Setup D has no leaves.
experiment.timing: In a real experiment: Keep the experiment and timer running while you measure. Read and record the data quickly at each planned time. Do not stop the timer to take measurements. This simulation pauses the picture to help you observe and record. The time you spend doing this is not part of the 30 simulated minutes.
ruler: Drag the ruler left or right to place it beside the leaf stalk. Its 0 mark stays at the water surface, so you cannot move it up or down. Read the height of the top of the red water trace. Enter the reading to one decimal place. The arrows beside each reading change it by 0.5 cm.
Each 10 minutes of simulated time takes about 3 seconds. This is a model for learning. It does not predict the exact results of a real experiment.

questions.heading: 3. What can this experiment tell us?
questions.sentence: We measured only the height of the red water trace. We did not measure water vapour (水汽) lost from the leaves. Which statement is most suitable?__________

options.text: The red water trace gives an indirect clue about water uptake and upward water transport. Its speed is not the rate of water loss from leaves, or the transpiration rate (蒸騰速率).
The upward speed of the water trace is the rate of water vapour (水汽) loss from leaves and can be used directly as the transpiration rate (蒸騰速率).
If the setups with leaves are faster than the setup without leaves, this fully proves that water vapour (水汽) is lost only through stomata (氣孔).

learning.heading: Learn about transpiration (蒸騰) from the red water trace
learning.points:
1. Transpiration (蒸騰) is the process in which water in a plant evaporates (蒸發) and is lost to the air as water vapour (水汽). Water vapour (水汽) mainly leaves through stomata (氣孔) in leaves and herbaceous stems (草本莖).
    1. Water evaporates (蒸發) from the water film (水膜) on the surface of mesophyll cells (葉肉細胞) and enters the air spaces (氣室) in the spongy mesophyll as water vapour (水汽). When the water vapour (水汽) concentration in the air spaces (氣室) is higher than in the air outside, water vapour (水汽) leaves the leaf through stomata (氣孔) by diffusion.
    2. When mesophyll cells (葉肉細胞) lose water, their water potential falls. They take in water from nearby cells by osmosis. This draws water out of the leaf's xylem vessels (木質導管) and creates transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力), which pulls water upwards through the stem's xylem vessels (木質導管).
  2. Under suitable conditions, such as enough water being available, higher light intensity (光強度) usually makes stomata (氣孔) open wider. Water vapour (水汽) then leaves the leaf faster by diffusion, so the transpiration rate (蒸騰速率) increases.
    Note: More light may also make the leaf's temperature rise, increasing transpiration (蒸騰) further. This investigation therefore assumes that all setups have the same temperature so we can compare the effect of light intensity (光強度).
  3. Transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力) keeps roots taking in water and moves water and dissolved minerals absorbed by the roots upwards through xylem vessels (木質導管) to the leaves.
learning.limit: See textbook section 11.1, pages 11-3 to 11-8. The red water trace gives evidence of water transport. Its upward speed is not a direct measure of the transpiration rate (蒸騰速率). Comparing celery with and without leaves alone also cannot prove the role of stomata (氣孔).

    <title id="structure-paper-title">Internal leaf structure and transpiration (蒸騰): water enters the leaf through xylem vessels (木質導管) and is lost as water vapour (水汽)</title>
    <desc id="structure-paper-desc">A three-dimensional view of part of a leaf cross-section. Palisade mesophyll cells (柵狀葉肉細胞) are packed closely together. Air spaces (氣室) lie between spongy mesophyll cells (海綿葉肉細胞), with water films (水膜) on the cell surfaces facing the air spaces (氣室). Upper and lower epidermal cells (表皮細胞) and guard cells (保衞細胞) contain vacuoles (液泡). An open stoma (氣孔) lies between the two guard cells (保衞細胞). In the vascular bundle (維管束), xylem (木質部) is above phloem (韌皮部). Xylem vessels (木質導管) in the stem and leaf are pink. Blue arrows show water transport and osmosis. Orange dashed arrows show water vapour (水汽) movement and diffusion. Orange numbers show the two steps of transpiration (蒸騰) through stomata (氣孔). cards.text: Water evaporates (蒸發) from the surfaces of mesophyll cells (葉肉細胞) into the air spaces (氣室).
Water vapour (水汽) in the air spaces (氣室) diffuses through stomata (氣孔) into the air.

processes.title: How transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力) forms

cards.text: Mesophyll cells (葉肉細胞) lose water, so their water potential falls.
Mesophyll cells (葉肉細胞) take in water from nearby cells by osmosis.
Water is drawn out of the xylem vessels (木質導管), creating transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力).

caption: Internal leaf structure and transpiration (蒸騰)
Orange numbers: transpiration (蒸騰) through stomata (氣孔) | Blue numbers: how transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力) forms
Enlarged view, not to scale. The celery stalk in this experiment is a petiole (葉柄). The stem shown here explains transport through xylem vessels (木質導管).

texts.observation: After some time, the red water trace extends upwards in some parts inside the celery stalk.
texts.hypothesis: There is no single answer. Your hypothesis should be testable (可測試的) by changing light intensity (光強度) and measuring the upward speed of the water trace.
texts.reason: Explain the link you expect between light and water transport. Your prediction does not have to match the final result.
texts.control: Compare setup D without leaves with setup B with leaves. Both have a lamp distance of 20 cm and the same other conditions. The main difference is whether leaves are present.
texts.design: Materials: 4 celery stalks, 4 desk lamps, 4 cups of red water, 4 rulers of 30 cm, 1 pair of scissors and 1 timer. Set the lamp distances for the three celery stalks with leaves to 10, 20 and 30 cm. Use the same lamp distance for the setup without leaves and one setup with leaves. Immerse each stalk 2 cm into the red water.

assumptions.reference: Temperature can also affect transpiration (蒸騰). This simulation keeps all setups at 25°C so light and temperature do not change together.

assumptions.text: Setups A, B and C have the same total leaf area.
assumptions.reference: Leaf area can affect water loss, so setups A, B and C with leaves should have the same total leaf area. Setup D without leaves provides a separate comparison.

assumptions.reference: Leaf area can affect water loss. Keep it the same when comparing light intensity (光強度).

assumptions.reference: Humidity (濕度) and air movement can also affect transpiration (蒸騰). Keep them the same when comparing light intensity (光強度).

Teacher marks
